entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

## imported-rows-leave-the-table | Done When 1: The table only shows nodes available to import. Already imported nodes are hidden.
proof.waitFor(() => { const rows = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog tbody tr')).map((row) => row.innerText); return rows.some((text) => text.includes('Cool bedrooms')) && !rows.some((text) => text.includes('Daylight exposure') || text.includes('Caffeine after noon')); }, { what: 'only the unimported claim in the table' })

## link-opens-the-page | Done When 10 and 11: After import, clicking an imported-node link in the result opens the imported node in Roam.
proof.waitFor(() => !proof.dialogs().length && Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.rm-title-display')).some((title) => proof.visible(title) && title.innerText.includes('Daylight exposure resets the circadian clock')), { what: 'the imported page open with the dialog closed' })

## reopen-hides-imported | Done When 1: The table only shows nodes available to import. Already imported nodes are hidden.
(() => { const rows = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog tbody tr')).map((row) => row.innerText); proof.assert(!rows.some((text) => text.includes('Daylight exposure') || text.includes('Caffeine after noon')), 'An imported claim is still in the table.'); })()

## qa-progress-bar-replaces-results-while | None
(() => { window.__feedWatch && window.__feedWatch.disconnect(); proof.assert(window.__feed.progress, 'No progress callout was shown.'); proof.assert(!window.__feed.resultWithProgress, 'The earlier result stayed on screen during the import.'); const results = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog .bp3-callout')).filter((item) => item.innerText.includes(' imported,')); proof.assert(results.length === 1, 'Expected one result, found ' + results.length); proof.assert(results[0].innerText.includes('Cool bedrooms') && !results[0].innerText.includes('Light therapy'), 'The result is not the new batch.'); })()

## qa-re-import-of-an-up-to-date-node-shows-as | None
(() => { const callout = proof.byText('.bp3-dialog .bp3-callout', 'Skipped nodes were already up to date'); proof.assert(callout, 'No result with skipped nodes.'); proof.assert(callout.querySelector('.bp3-heading').innerText.trim() === '2 imported, 1 skipped, 0 failed', 'The title is ' + callout.querySelector('.bp3-heading').innerText.trim()); const links = Array.from(callout.querySelectorAll('li a')).map((link) => link.innerText.trim()); ['PKC - Skip claim', 'PKSRC - Sleep hygiene review', 'PKE - Late meals cut deep sleep - [[PKSRC - Sleep hygiene review]]'].forEach((title) => proof.assert(links.includes(title), 'No link for ' + title + ' in ' + JSON.stringify(links))); })()

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

content.text:
No, it wasn't what we want, and you were right. I've fixed it, and all 20 proof cases now pass in Roam. The fix is committed locally as `104615e` but **not pushed yet**.

**What was wrong:** Roam's own `site.css` breaks Tailwind's `flex` class in two ways.
- **Every `flex` element stretches to fill its parent.** In the footer, the button group took all the space, so Close and Import selected sat right against the node count.
- **Every element can shrink to zero height.** The search row collapsed when the list was long, so the input stuck out of the top and got cut off. That's your screenshot.
- **The column headers weren't sticky,** so they scrolled away with the rows.

**The fix, all in `DiscoverSharedNodesDialog.tsx`:**
- `flex-none` on the search row, the progress and result boxes, and the footer buttons. Tailwind loads after Roam's CSS, so this wins.
- Only the table area scrolls now, and the column header row stays on top.
- Result links now have an `href`, so the keyboard can reach them. That was Devin's 🟡 finding.

Prettier, eslint and tsc all pass.

**The proof kit:** I added a check that scrolls the rows and confirms the search field, column headers and footer stay in place. It failed on the PR's head commit and passes on the fix. While running it I hit a second failure: relations never imported, with the message "Missing author". That came from the test database, not the PR. The test authors weren't members of their own spaces, so the importing graph couldn't see them. I fixed that in the kit's setup and told the other session that owns the harness. I also rewrote the kit's text to the wording rules it asked for.

I checked frames from the video myself: the empty table, a long list scrolled, a failed import with a warning, shift-click into the sidebar, and the relation-failure message. Nothing else looked wrong.

- Report: `/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/output/proof/eng-2296-2026-10-07T11-51-33-388Z/report.md`
- Video (silent): `/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/output/proof/eng-2296-2026-10-07T11-51-33-388Z/eng-2296.mp4`

**Before review:**
1. **Push `104615e`?** It's the exact commit the proof ran on.
2. **The branch is 33 commits behind main.** That's the only reason the Entire Gates check fails. It merges without conflicts.
3. **Devin's 🔴 finding is still open:** a failed relation import can't be retried. I recommend a "Retry relations" button in the result box. I'm waiting on your call.
4. After the push: `/pre-pr-review` on the new head, update the PR body (it still says "not tested in Roam" and "Loom pending"), and post the report and video on the PR. I'll ask before posting anything.

I'm planning to merge origin/main cleanly with a simple default commit message, then add a flex-none class to the StoredRelationsWarning component in the dialog, and finally adjust the refresh command's gating logic so it only appears when sync or node sharing is enabled.

Now I'm working through the refresh gating logic more carefully — refresh should be available whenever import is available, meaning isSyncEnabled() should be the trigger, combined with the existing isNodeSharingEnabled() check to preserve current sharing users. I'm updating the condition in initializeObserversAndListeners to check for sharingEnabled or syncEnabled before reading imported source identity, and I need to verify whether refreshImportedNode has its own gating requirements around node sharing.

For the retry relations button, I'm adding state to track whether the relations import failed, setting it in the catch block of importSelectedNodes, and rendering a retry button that re-runs importSharedRelations when clicked, with a loading indicator while it retries.

I'm defining an importRelations helper that takes the client, calls importSharedRelations with the space ID and imported RIDs, clears the failure flag on success, and sets the failure flag plus shows an internal error toast on failure — this gets reused by both the initial import and the retry handler, which fetches its own client via getLoggedInClient. I'm deciding where to surface the retry UI, likely embedding a message and button directly inside the ImportResultsSummary callout rather than a separate component.

I'm adding a conditional block at the bottom of the summary that shows a warning message with a small retry button when relationsFailed is true, switching the callout's intent to warning in that case. I also need to reset relationsFailed at the start of a new import or node load, and figure out how to disable the import/retry buttons appropriately so they can't be triggered simultaneously.

Now I'm thinking through how to prove the retry case actually works — the existing broken fixture (rel-3-4 with NULL author) is a permanent failure, so retrying it would just fail again. To demonstrate success, I'd need a step that fixes the underlying data between the failure and the retry, which means using a REST call with the service key to patch the record directly rather than relying on browser-side SQL.

Since the fixture resets author_id to NULL on every run via ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, I can build a case that fixes the author via that REST patch, clicks "Retry relations," waits for the button to disappear, and verifies the relation now exists and the retry button is gone.

This is a QA-style manual case, so I'll add it as "s-relation-import-after-node-import" and mark it hand-written/approved. For the refresh gating proof — testing whether "DG: Refresh all imported nodes" appears in the command palette when node sharing is off — I realize I can't easily toggle that flag mid-session since it's registered at load time, so I'll leave that gating untested by a proof case and just note it as a unit-level concern instead.

Actually let me double check whether refresh logic even depends on node sharing by reading refreshImportedNode before assuming it needs separate verification.

Then my remaining steps are straightforward: run lint/prettier/tsc checks, commit, push, force-rebuild, verify frames, do the pre-PR review, update the PR body, and reply on the Devin/Codex threads — but I should still ask before posting PR comments since that's required by the post stage, even though sid said to push everything. I'll prepare it all and ask once at the end. Starting now by merging main.

Both recommendations are approved, so I'll proceed in order: merge main to clear Entire Gates, add refresh alongside import, add a Retry relations button with a proof case, then rerun the full proof and review. Starting with the merge now.

content.text:
<skill-prompt>
Run a pre-PR review of the current change set. This is NOT a checklist to ponder — it is a sequence of verification steps with pass/fail outcomes. You must actually run the greps/traces; "I believe this is fine" without having looked is a failed step. Built from an autopsy of 97 real reviewer comments (2026-03→07) — 46 violated rules a previous skill already "had" but never enforced; recall is not verification — and refreshed 2026-08-28 against the 2026-07→08 corpus (~200 human review comments across sid's and teammates' PRs).

Required reading before step 1 (both live in `<repo-root>/.claude/context/`, repo root `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph` — reachable by absolute path from any worktree):
- `engineering-context.md` — team philosophies and hard-learned lessons (the *why* behind every check below)
- `db-domain-invariants.md` — current schema/data-layer facts (the data-layer pass checks the diff against every entry)

## Mode gate (run FIRST, before Step 0)

Decide which mode this run needs. This is a judgment call you make from evidence — not a rule to apply mechanically, and not something to take on faith from the dispatching prompt (dispatch prompts are written fresh each run and can get this wrong in either direction):
- Evidence a full pass already ran on this PR: a previous run's line-anchored annotations posted on the PR, existing review threads answering a prior findings report, or the dispatcher naming a last-reviewed SHA.
- Default when a full pass ran and the commits since only answer review feedback: Re-review mode below.
- A full pass on a follow-up push can still be the right call when there's genuine reason — the delta added surface beyond the feedback (the escape hatch below), the base moved under the branch, prior coverage looks doubtful or stale, or enough rounds have accumulated that the whole PR deserves fresh eyes. If you judge that, run full and say why.
- The first line of your output states the chosen mode and the reasoning — that's what keeps the choice reviewable, whichever way it goes.

## Step 0 — Inventory

The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. Never review only the latest commits: reviewers see the whole PR, and code that landed on the branch before this run is still your surface. (Exception: Re-review mode below.) Classify changed files:
- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config

Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.

## Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)

If a full pre-pr-review already ran on this PR and this run covers a follow-up push (fixes after a review round or a previous run's findings), do NOT repeat the full sequence:

- Change set = `git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD` — the commits since the state the previous round covered, not the whole PR again.
- **Findings closure first.** For every finding from the previous run and every reviewer/bot comment since: re-run the SPECIFIC check that produced it and report fixed / not-fixed / deferred+ticket per item. A fix claimed without re-verification is a failed step; a UI fix additionally gets re-driven (existing rule).
- Run steps 1–3 mechanically on the delta only, with Step 0's DATA/FRONTEND scoping applied to the delta. Step 4 shrinks to: every new hunk maps to the review feedback or the ticket, and the bot-comment gate on comments the new push attracted.
- Skip re-reading the context docs unless the delta touches DATA/FRONTEND files and they aren't already in context.
- Escape hatch: if the "follow-up" adds new surface (rebase onto a moved base, new feature code, a refactor beyond what was asked), it is not a re-review — run the full sequence on the full PR diff.

## Step 1 — Mechanical sweeps (always run; each is an action, not a question)

1a. **Reuse gate.** List every NEW named thing in the diff (function, type, component, constant, enum, marker string). For each, run a grep across `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src`, and sibling files for the core operation or shape. Report what you searched and what you found. A new thing duplicating an existing one is a finding. Special case: every inline string-literal union (`"X" | "Y"`) gets its members grepped in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`; members matching a generated enum → must use `Enums<"…">`.

1b. **Justification sweep.** For every added default value, optional prop/field, state variable, fallback (`?? x`, `|| x`), and kept-through-refactor line: name the concrete code path that exercises it. Trace return types through call sites — if a function always returns `T`, a `?? fallback` at its call site is dead code; say so. No path → finding: delete it.

1c. **Literal hoist.** Repeated or typo-prone string literals (prop keys, selectors, attribute names, ids) appearing more than once or shared with other files → must be a named constant defined once.

1d. **Type honesty.** For every `as`, `any`, `unknown`, `!` (non-null assertion), `?.`, `void`, and `|| default` in the diff: can the value actually be null/absent there? Verify against the type at its source, don't guess. Assertion where a guard or upstream fix is possible → finding. A `!` that must survive gets an inline comment saying why it's safe — mdroidian flags every bare `!` (#1329, #1324).

1e. **Explainability.** For each hunk: one sentence, why is this here in service of the ticket? Reorderings, reformats, removals, and leftover scaffolding you can't explain → finding: revert.

1f. **Call-graph pass (review the resulting system, not the diff).** For every exported symbol added or modified, and every function parameter added: grep ALL call sites across `apps/` and `packages/` and read them. Findings:
- a parameter that only one caller supplies (or that every caller could omit) → internalize or remove it
- a wrapper that after this change only renames/forwards or adds one trivial field → collapse it into its caller
- an export with zero external consumers → unexport
- an existing caller whose behavior silently changes (check what it did with the old return shape — e.g. did it append `Z` to a timestamp you now normalize?)
Reviewers read the post-state code, not the diff; a hunk that looks justified in isolation can leave the system with dead indirection.

1g. **Comment audit.** List every comment line ADDED by the diff. Delete any that restates the code or narrates the change — "Claude, chill on the comments" is a real review quote, left twice (#1222, #1321), and "some unnecessary comments here" a third time (#1292). A comment referencing context not present in the file (another PR, a discussion, another platform's behavior) either becomes self-contained or dies: reviewers reply "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" to comments they can't parse cold (#1315, #1292, #1284). Keep only comments stating a constraint the code can't show.

1h. **Second-lookup check.** For every new fetch, map-build, `.find`, or helper lookup: trace where its input data was constructed — was the looked-up value already present there (on the row, the batch, an upstream type)? If yes → thread the field through the pipeline types instead of re-deriving downstream. (#1266: importer re-fetched `schema_id` that `SharedNode` already carried; #1317: `getFormatByNodeTypeUid()` second lookup when `matchingNodeType.format` was in hand at the construction site.)

1i. **Workflow injection (only if `.github/workflows/` changed).** Any `${{ inputs.* }}` / `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolated directly into a `run:` script is shell injection — pass it through `env:` and use a quoted variable, validated against a fully anchored pattern (#1253).

## Step 2 — Data-layer pass (only if DATA files changed)

2a. Open `db-domain-invariants.md` and check the diff against EVERY entry. For each entry state: applies / doesn't apply / VIOLATION. Do not summarize the file — walk it.

2b. **Provenance trace.** For every value read from a PostgREST response or datalog result used in the diff: name the source column, grep its type in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/*.sql`, then judge the code handling it (timestamps are the known killer — naive UTC, no `Z`).

2c. **Query review.** For every `.from(...)` chain (new or modified): required domain filters present (arity, is_schema, variant)? Any client-side `.filter`/`.find`/sort the request could express? Payload columns in a listing path? Paginated with a unique total order? Inside a loop that should be batched?

2d. **Contract check.** New/changed shared types: required-vs-optional modeled from real cases (does every producer actually supply it)? Identity carried once (RID) not duplicated decomposed? Consistent with `crossAppContracts.ts` and with what the Obsidian side already assumes — check its consumer code, don't assume.

2e. **Converter matrix.** A field added or renamed on a cross-app contract or schema type must be handled in EVERY converter, BOTH directions, or explicitly deferred with a ticket named in the PR. Enumerate the cells and mark each handled/deferred: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`, and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side). maparent asked for the missing direction on #1316 AND #1317: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions."

2f. **Flag-gated writes.** For every new DB write path: which user-visible flag or action authorizes it? Sync flag off ⇒ the user expects NO DB communication; a silent maintenance write (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out in the PR, and its outcome reports to PostHog — never a user toast (#1332).

## Step 3 — Frontend pass (only if FRONTEND files changed)

Check against the frontend lessons in `engineering-context.md`, mechanically:
- grep the diff for `style=`, `class-[`/`-[` arbitrary values, hex colors → Tailwind-scale violations
- grep for `window.roamAlphaAPI` legacy paths (sync `.q`, `async.backend`) → current-API violations
- settings writes → must go through block-props accessors, preserving the store gate
- new UI elements → which flag gates them (including EXISTING flags the new surface must respect, e.g. `autoCanvasRelations` on #1272); user-facing failures → PostHog + toast, not `console.error`
- names: every new variable/setter/label states exactly what it holds or does; UI labels reuse existing product vocabulary ("discourse context", not an invented synonym — #1255)
- grep the diff for positional child access on settings/config trees (`tree[3]`, `.children[0]`) → look up by key with `getSubTree`; position compiles today and silently writes to the wrong parent after any reorder (#1302)
- persisted/saved data stores stable IDs (shape id, uid), never display names — names are UI-only and subject to change (#1222: save `frameShapeId`, not `frameName`)
- `Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary: excluded from user-selectable type lists (#1298), never name-resolved to/from a remote schema, never creatable as configured types (#1331 was blocked on exactly this; #1272 applied the same rule on canvas)
- a panel that replaces or extends existing UI matches it pixel-wise — proportions, selected-tab highlight, centering; reviewers screenshot-compare against the original (#1255, #1272). Empty states key on the right condition (no relation *instances* ≠ no relation *types*, #1255)
- user-facing strings use user vocabulary — a toast saying "backfilled" is a finding; internal bookkeeping reports to PostHog only (#1332)

## Step 4 — Process gate

- Every hunk maps to this PR's ticket; unrelated changes → revert or explicitly annotate. Out-of-scope improvements a reviewer might request → pre-empt by naming them in the PR with a Linear ticket ("X is deferred to ENG-YYYY").
- **One problem, ~<500 lines.** A PR solves a single problem in under ~500 changed lines before tests (mdroidian's stated bar, #1222). Real drive-by bug fixes split into their own ticket — and get fixed at their source layer (a roamjs-components bug is fixed in roamjs-components, not patched locally).
- **Bot-comment gate.** Before requesting human review: every codex/graphite/devin comment is either fixed or answered with why-not, and resolved. mdroidian's first pass is frequently just "See codex comments" / "address the bot reviews … and click resolve" (#1257, #1309, #1320) — an unresolved bot thread costs a full review round-trip.
- **Chain coverage.** For a PR in a stacked or sibling-ticket chain: does the union of this PR + named sibling tickets cover both platforms and both data directions? "This only handles Obsidian-origin — where's Roam-origin?" is maparent's most repeated 07–08 comment (#1267, #1269, #1316). Name the gap and the ticket that owns it in the PR before he does.
- **Guard removals are argued in the PR.** Removing an existence check or gate: state the cases it protected and why each is now safe (idempotent re-upsert, upstream guarantee). #1280's check removal survived review, but through a 3-comment thread that one PR annotation would have preempted.
- **Refactor/extraction parity table.** If this PR moves or extracts code (util → shared package, file split, API swap): produce a table of old symbol → new symbol → `identical` or `changed: <why>`. Every not-1:1 replacement is a decision the reviewer WILL ask about ("could you walk through those decisions?") — enumerate them before they do. The table goes in the PR description.
- Runtime proof: does this change have a surface a unit test can't exercise (UI, load-order, multi-user)? If yes, a demo is REQUIRED, not noted (`/demo-handoff`). If the diff touches DOM observers, drag/hover interactions, or rendered Roam surfaces: emit a **regression matrix** — surfaces (main window, right sidebar, left sidebar, Kanban, query-builder link/embed/render views, canvas) × content shapes (single-line, multiline/wrapping, nested references, page titles) — marking which cells this change can affect; the demo must drive every affected cell, with the mouse cursor visible in the recording, and any bug you claim fixed must be re-driven by you after the fix. Video quality bar (#1298): signal each state change visually (a quick caption/toast — "before fix" / "on branch"), don't carry it in narration alone, and cut narration that states the obvious ("every relation has a source and destination" earned a 🙄 from mdroidian).
- Reviewer context: list the bullets the PR description must contain (what was removed and why, temporary code, decisions made, deferrals + tickets). Test: could someone review this without asking a question?
- **Inherited decisions carry breadcrumbs.** Any code that exists because of a review decision on a PREVIOUS PR (a reviewer's direction, a contract agreed in another thread) gets a draft line-comment citing that source ("per maparent on #1214: local IDs may already be RIDs"). Without the breadcrumb the next reviewer re-litigates it.

## Output

1. **Findings**, ranked by severity, each: file:line — what — why it matters (cite the context-doc entry or the verification step that failed) — concrete fix.
2. **Verification log** — one line per mechanical step: what you ran/checked and the outcome. This proves the steps happened; a review with findings but no log is invalid.
2b. **Draft PR annotations** — ready-to-post, line-anchored comments explaining every non-obvious decision (guidepost style: what this block does and why, inherited-decision citations, parity-table deltas). Proven repeatedly: #1214, and in 07–08 reviewers replied to annotations in-thread and accepted the argument (#1280 "I accept this argument. Approving.", #1331). Also annotate every LARGE removal or moved block ("this was refactored into abc.ts") — mdroidian asked for exactly this on #1320. Posting them is part of finishing the PR, not optional polish.
2c. All reviewer-facing prose this skill emits — PR description bullets, draft annotations, deferral notes, parity tables — follows the team writing style skill at `<repo-root>/.claude/skills/discourse-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md` (mdroidian's #1278): lead with the point, one term per concept, replace vague verbs ("handle", "support") with the specific behavior, no em dashes, shortest version that keeps the nuance.

These are forecasts to fix or preempt in the PR description, not instructions to please anyone.
4. If a pass is clean, say so explicitly. Do not manufacture findings; ~11% of historical review comments were not catchable pre-PR (product/1:1 context) — surface open questions instead of contorting.

Anti-weasel rules: no "not harmful, just unnecessary" (unnecessary = delete), no "acceptable for consistency" (a no-op kept for symmetry is cargo-culting), no noting facts without stating the conclusion they imply. If you have the information that leads to a finding, state the finding.

on:
  pull_request:
    types:
      - opened
      - synchronize
    paths:
      - "apps/roam/**"
      - "packages/tailwind-config/**"
      - "packages/utils/**"
      - "packages/database/**"
      - "packages/ui/**"
env:
  BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN }}
  DISCOURSE_GRAPH_BUILD_COMMIT: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
  DISCOURSE_GRAPH_BUILD_BRANCH: ${{ github.head_ref }}

    steps:

        with:
